THE RULE BEING AUDITED (Brandon, 2026-10-31, now in docs/contributor-guide.md): world-model logic lives in packages/worldkeeper, not in storygame. A rule that reads or changes only world state (parents, containment, kinds, reach, visibility, seats, companions, axes, hidden/unplaced flags, names and aliases of entities) is a `World` method in packages/worldkeeper/src/worldkeeper/model.py with tests in packages/worldkeeper/tests/. storygame/runtime/world_model.py only adapts the story package and facts to worldkeeper; other modules call World methods and never walk the tree themselves. Code that needs the StoryPackage (scenes, NPC labels, knowledge, pacing), prose or text matching for narration, or a model call stays in storygame. worldkeeper must stay story-agnostic: it may not import storygame or know any story's ids or vocabulary.

FILES YOU AUDIT:
- /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/storygame/runtime/item_facts.py

WHAT TO DO.
1. Read the worldkeeper library first: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/packages/worldkeeper/src/worldkeeper/model.py (the `World` class and its helpers) and the README in packages/worldkeeper. Know every existing World method so you never propose one that already exists under another name.
2. In each audited file, find EVERY function or method that calls a World method (world.parent, world.is_a, world.children, world.area, world.name, world.place, world.companions, etc.) or reads `wk_` facts. Use `grep -n` to be exhaustive. Read each one in full.
3. Give each a verdict:
   - move: the whole function depends only on world state (a World plus plain ids/strings as arguments). It should become a World method (or a worldkeeper helper) and its storygame callers call that instead.
   - split: part of it is pure world logic (e.g. a loop that walks parents to find the enclosing container, a reachability or visibility test, a kind test chain) and part needs the StoryPackage, prose, or a model call. Name exactly the lines that are pure world logic.
   - stay: it only calls existing World methods as a client (no tree walking of its own) or the world logic is inseparable from story/prose/model logic. Say why.
   Be strict and concrete: a single `world.parent(x)` lookup used to decide narration is a client call (stay); a `while` loop over parents, a recursive descent over children, or a reimplementation of a rule World already has (e.g. its own visibility or containment walk) is world logic. Also flag DUPLICATES: storygame code that recomputes what an existing World method already computes; say which method.
4. For move/split also give: proposed_world_method (a signature such as `World.enclosing_container(self, entity_id: str) -> str | None` and one sentence on its contract), callers (every `file:line` in storygame that calls the function; find them with grep across storygame/ and tests/), and needs_story_package: false (the moved part must not need the package). If the moved part would need a package concept, say what plain data could be passed in instead, or mark it stay.
5. Note risks: hidden behaviour differences (ordering, None handling, groups, companions, seats, part_of, under) a mover must preserve.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: write valid JSON to the report path above, shaped as {"group": "item-facts", "findings": [ {"file": "storygame/runtime/x.py" (repo-relative, exactly one of the audited files), "function": "name as defined in the file (for methods, the method name)", "lines": "start-end", "verdict": "move|split|stay", "world_state_read": "which world state it reads or changes", "reason": "why this verdict, citing lines", "pure_world_lines": "for split only", "duplicates_world_method": "name or empty", "proposed_world_method": "...", "callers": ["file:line"], "needs_story_package": false, "risks": "..."} ], "summary": "3-6 sentences"}. Every audited file must have at least one finding (list World-calling functions even when the verdict is stay). Function names must exist in the file you cite; the check parses the files and rejects invented names.
DONE WHEN the report validates: `/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/scripts/ringer/worldkeeper-boundary/check_audit.py /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/worldkeeper-boundary-audit/item-facts.json storygame/runtime/item_facts.py` prints PASS.
